title: HC Mike LaFleur Postgame Press Conference | Week 7 vs. Denver Broncos
headline: LaFleur backs Jacoby Brissett to start next week, calls Trey McBride and Michael Wilson 'huge reasons' the offense can turn around, and owns red-zone and clock-management mistakes in a Week 7 loss to Denver.
summary: LaFleur said the loss to Denver came down to finishing: too many penalties, missed opportunities, and red-zone failures that he called correctable but not yet fixed. He took responsibility for the sack in the final drive, saying he chose to save clock instead of running from the one-yard line and then called a pass that put the offense back into a tough spot. He defended the fourth-and-goal decision, saying he went for the tight game because Denver had been struggling to score and his defense was playing well, and said the call might differ in other games. He said the offense's problems are collective, refused to single out individuals, and said Jacoby Brissett was not the reason, while acknowledging Brissett was under pressure and took hits, with the protection needing a quicker click. He praised Trey McBride and Michael Wilson as 'studs' who would be key to flipping the season, and said Bam Knight's uncaught end-zone target was a collective miss with an opportunity to come later. He said the team played better than its previous two games but still needs to play consistently good football at home, and he will review the tape on the offensive line, including Hayden Conner, before judging it further.

topics.detail: LaFleur said the red-zone problems were new to the team a week ago and are correctable, citing failed progressions, a draw that drew a holding penalty, and an earlier cover-zero look. He said the team needs to actually execute the fixes.

He took ownership of the sack that hurt the final drive, saying he prioritized clock over a run from the one-yard line. He also defended going for it on fourth-and-two early, saying he wanted a tight game and the call reflected the expected low-scoring game.

LaFleur praised Denver as a well-coached team that is 5-2 and getting its offense back on track. He said Arizona's defense gave up explosive plays early, including a scramble by Bo Nix, which loosened the defense for later drives.

He said the team had too many penalties and too many missed chances to make plays, and that the offense needs to play better at home, where he said it has not yet shown the same consistency it showed on the road.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Post-game Press Conference | Week 7 | Falcons vs. 49ers
headline: Penix threw three TDs and Kendal Daniels returned from a hospital scare to play and make a late interception; Stefanski praised both and the Falcons won their first home game.
summary: Stefanski opened by crediting a +4 turnover margin and said the team played fast and physical against a good opponent. He called Kendal Daniels' week remarkable: Daniels was at the hospital a week earlier, then played, called the defense, and made a late interception, and Stefanski gave him a game ball. He credited Michael Penix Jr. for a strong day with three touchdown passes and said the quarterback read the defense well. He praised the medical staff for getting Daniels back on track quickly and said the plan was to avoid holding the ball against a strong rush team. Stefanski highlighted Jessie Bates III's two big second-half plays and said the offensive line, receivers, and quarterback all contributed to the pressure numbers, crediting OC Tommy's game plan. He said the tight ends are used game to game across several personnel groupings and praised Nick Muse's goal-line route. He also praised Maason Smith's pass rush and Drake London's blocking and hard yards.

title: Jesse Minter Recaps Loss to Bengals
headline: Lamar Jackson's status for next week is unresolved; Minter says the team will sort it out over the next couple of days.
summary: Minter credited the Bengals after a 35-13 loss, calling it a tale of two halves. He felt the Ravens started well but did not capitalize on enough first-half chances to build separation. In the second half, Cincinnati made early plays, gained momentum, and the Ravens could not get it back. He said the team is too reliant on momentum and needs to stay more even-keeled. He put the blame on all three phases and said the defense missed tackles, allowing explosive plays and short-yardage gains to turn into longer ones. He was concerned about the run game's inefficiency over the last few weeks and said the staff must find better answers on the offensive line. He said the Bengals' adjustments under pressure came mainly from the Ravens failing to win on normal downs, which left them in too many third-and-long situations. On the injury questions, he had no update on the one about "Vegas" (the caption is likely garbled). On Lamar Jackson, he said the staff would decide over the next couple of days whether he could practice and play next week. He also said the offense needs better plans and adjustments for the second half.

injuries.detail: Injured in a recent game; Minter said the staff will determine over the next couple of days whether he practices and can play next week.

signals.claim: Availability for next week will be determined over the next couple of days, with no firm answer yet.
signals.note: His practice participation this week is the key indicator for whether he plays next week, which matters a great deal for Ravens offense projections.
signals.quote: Yeah, I think over the next couple days we'll figure that out.

topics.detail: Minter said he is concerned about the Ravens' run-game inefficiency in recent weeks and that they need to find better answers, including on the offensive line.
Minter said the defense missed too many tackles in the second half, letting Cincinnati turn short gains into big plays. He said he would review the tape.
Minter said the team rides momentum too much and needs to stay even-keeled. He said the team controls its own mentality and will keep working on it through tough conversations.

Minter said Cincinnati's changes against pressure, including short throws and corner plays, exploited the Ravens' failure to win on early downs. He said the defense will review several adjustments made at halftime.

title: Dave Canales speaks after Sunday’s game against Buccaneers
headline: Panthers lose to Bucs after 22 points off turnovers; Taylor Moton is out for a while with a fibula fracture and his season is uncertain.
summary: Canales was disappointed in the loss and said the turnovers, including two interceptions, a sack-fumble that became a touchdown, a dropped punt, and a blocked kick, gave Tampa Bay 22 points and put Carolina in a hole it could not climb out of. He credited the Bucs' run game and game plan, saying their patience and varied run schemes found voids, and said the Panthers' own tackling and gap fits, along with a few missed tackles, let backs get into space. He said the pass rush and stunts up front were a problem, and that the protection breakdowns and the sack-fumble need film review. On Taylor Moton, he said the tackle has a fibula fracture after being rolled up on, will be out for a while, and the full extent and timeline await further workup. Canales said Bryce Young stayed positive and encouraging on the sideline, but the turnovers made for a bad day. He called the week's preparation focused and said the team had a quick turnaround with a Monday meeting. He would not say whether Moton's injury is season-ending.

injuries.detail: Fibula fracture suffered when he was rolled up on during the game; expected to be out for a while, with the full extent pending further evaluation. Season-ending status not confirmed.

signals.claim: Will be out for a while with a fibula fracture; extent of injury still being determined
signals.note: Starting tackle's absence hurts the offensive line and Bryce Young's protection, and a season-ending result would be a major loss for the line.
signals.quote: Timo is going to be out for a while.

signals.claim: Stayed positive and encouraging on the sideline and is ready to move on from the game despite the turnovers
signals.note: Turnovers and heavy pressure are a concern for his weekly floor, but the coach says his mindset is sound.
signals.quote: He was encouraging his teammates

topics.detail: Canales cited two interceptions, a sack-fumble returned for a touchdown, a dropped punt that led to points, and a blocked kick as the main reasons for the early deficit.
He said stunts and movement up front were not handled well and that Tampa Bay brought pressure the Panthers had not seen before, which he expects other teams to copy.
He credited the Bucs' patient, varied run game and said Carolina had missed gap fits, containment, and tackles, though the calls were good.
The team had a Monday meeting to review critical variables, and the coach said players must move quickly into recovery and preparation.
Canales praised the Bucs' game plan and execution and said quarterback Baker Mayfield took care of the ball and extended drives.

title: Zac Taylor Speaks Following Week 7 Victory In Baltimore | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Ja'Marr Chase had zero first-half catches but was a major second-half factor in the 35-13 comeback win over Baltimore; Erick All (knee) is questionable and Bryan Cook is back.
summary: Zac Taylor said the first half was a failure on third downs on both sides of the ball, with the offense never finding rhythm and the defense allowing conversions on most third downs, though the defense held Baltimore to two field goals. At halftime the staff emphasized composure and the players led the adjustment, and the team scored five straight touchdowns while the defense forced five straight stops, including a turnover and fourth-down stops. Taylor said the offense got into a rhythm by leaning on the passing game's basics and productive runs, and he credited Ja'Marr Chase's halftime leadership and his big second-half production after no first-half catches. He praised the edge rushers and the back-end coverage, noting Baltimore's quarterbacks create explosive plays and the team had to answer them. Taylor said the win reaffirms the team's identity but is only one of 17 games, so the focus shifts quickly to Tennessee. On injuries, he said Erick All (knee) and a player he called Doug (quad) are still being evaluated, and Bryan Cook returned to play.

title: Todd Monken Press Conference at Titans: October 25th, 2026
headline: Judkins is back and the run game improved, Watson closed out another comeback drive, and KC Concepcion's slant-route usage is a growing factor.
summary: Monken called the 27-24 win over Tennessee a team win that was far from perfect, especially the slow start and the turnovers, which he said felt much like the previous week. He credited the defense's goal-line stand and a Denzel pick, and said the offense was better in most measurables except turnovers, including running the ball, first downs, pass efficiency, third downs, and red zone scoring. He praised Deshaun Watson's composure and said it was the most complete game of the season for him, though he noted one slant turnover that was on the receiver's route. Monken said the offense ran the ball better and that getting Quinshon Judkins back, along with players getting more time together, made a real difference. He said the staff does not plan targets ahead of time and that the success of KC Concepcion was a product of the game flow and two-minute drives. He said the team faced a four-down front this week, which matches its daily practice look, and that it wants to be multi-dimensional rather than one-dimensional. He praised Concepcion as humble and competitive, and he thanked the Cleveland crowd. The focus now shifts to Pittsburgh.

title: Campbell on Week 7 performance
headline: Goff, St. Brown, and Dorsey all earned praise, and Campbell said Dorsey will see more defensive snaps going forward.
summary: Campbell called the Week 7 win over Green Bay a good result that came mainly from the defense, which he described as the story of the game. He said the secondary wasn't perfect but played physically, and he credited the front for disruption and Khalil Dorsey for stepping in with big downfield plays. He was frustrated that two turnovers and a failed fourth-down attempt let the offense waste momentum, though he said the offense recovered and finished with a drive that ended in Gibbs carrying the ball with one second left. Campbell praised Jared Goff for managing the game and taking care of the football, and he credited the offensive line for protecting him well. He said the defense's confidence is rising as players trust their help, and he said the team is now moving on to Minnesota. He also discussed a returning player who was back from injury and still shaking off rust, and he said the team was careful to manage his workload in the first half.

Campbell praised the coverage units and D.J. Wonnum's blocked field goal. A player went down awkwardly late in the game and Campbell said he should be fine, though the player was not named.

title: Shane Steichen: Colts at Vikings postgame
headline: Steichen backs Daniel Jones with no QB change planned, and Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan split the carries as the run game led the gameplan.
summary: Steichen said the Colts planned to establish the run against Minnesota, so Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan handled most of the carries, which he felt were effective. He said the passing game fell short of expectations, citing Minnesota's pressure, quick throws, and max-protection situations where backs had to block and outlets were covered. He credited Vikings safety Harrison Smith for a key play and said the Vikings mixed coverages and pressure looks effectively. He praised the defense for a fourth-and-one stop on the first drive and several third-down stops, while saying it had fought to hold Minnesota to a field goal late. On the kicking game, he defended kicker Spencer Shrader's (listed as Spence) confidence, saying the missed attempts were a bad day rather than a concern. Asked about quarterback Daniel Jones, Steichen said he has not considered a change and has a lot of faith in him, while noting the late interception. He said he would get more information from the doctors on quarterback injuries and addressed the team's injuries at the start, but the exact players were unclear in the captions. He closed by stressing effort and that the team will keep working toward the next game.

title: HC Jeff Hafley - Oct 25 | Postgame Press Conference
headline: Hafley called Malik Willis's performance his best game and praised his decisiveness; no injury news was given.
summary: Hafley said the team needed to learn how to win, and the Dolphins finally got their first victory with a 28-25 win over the Jets at home. He credited the offensive line and the run game, and said the team got physical up front. He praised Malik Willis, saying he played his best game, was decisive, got rid of the ball quickly, took care of the football, and made good decisions. He said Willis is still developing, since six games amounts to roughly a rookie starter's workload. Hafley also praised Zayne Anderson for a goal-line play, describing him as a backup who can be counted on. He said the defense had many uncharacteristic missed assignments, especially in man coverage, and that it will need to clean that up on tape. He said the team wants a physical back who can close out games, and he said the late clock management and two-minute situations need more work. He admitted he could have made a better fourth-down call, even though the fourth-down attempt succeeded.

signals.claim: Played his best game of the season and was decisive, competing at a high level
signals.note: Strong praise and a clear sign of growing trust suggests he keeps his starting role and gains confidence in the offense.
signals.quote: I thought Malik played his best game and that was really cool to see.

signals.claim: Is currently a backup who the team can count on to come in when needed
signals.note: His role has shifted from rotational starter to backup, so his fantasy value depends on any injury or snap changes.

Hafley said he trusted the offensive line and went for it on fourth and one to seal the game, though he admitted he could have called it better.
Hafley said the team wants a physical back who can close out games and wear down opponents, with gap and direct run concepts suited to the offensive line.

title: Kevin O’Connell on Advancing to 6-0, Harrison Smith’s Interception & Blake Cashman’s Sacks
headline: Blake Cashman is playing at an elite level and gets weekly game balls; Myles Price and Jordan Addison are cleared, and Aaron Jones's knee status is unclear.
summary: O'Connell opened by praising the crowd and the win, calling Harrison Smith's late interception a special moment. He said the offense left plays on the field, with nine explosive plays but too many penalties, inefficient runs, and third-and-long situations. He was confident the unit is close and said the goal is to stack positive plays. He took ownership of a costly early play-calling sequence after a momentum-changing return. He praised Blake Cashman's pre-snap communication, blitzing, and instinctive plays, and said he has earned a game ball each week. On Kyler Murray, he said the staff is working to find more ways to activate his running. He emphasized winning the field position battle, which he said was won by five or six yards, along with avoiding turnovers and penalties. On injuries, Myles Price returned after a stinger, Jordan Addison cleared a concussion evaluation, and Aaron Jones had his knee evaluated with no clear update given.

title: Kellen Moore recaps Saints' loss to Steelers in Paris | Saints-Steelers Postgame | 2026 NFL Week 7
headline: Saints' run game managed just 18 yards on 17 carries in the Paris loss; a bye week follows, and CJ Donaldson and Justin Reid are dealing with concussion-related issues.
summary: Moore opened by thanking the French hosts and calling the Paris event a great experience, but said the Saints lost a close game they had chances to win. He pointed to the run game as the main problem: 17 carries for 18 yards, which made the offense too pass-heavy and left the Saints unable to sustain drives. He said the bye week will be used for full evaluation, but he would not commit to specific changes yet. Moore also noted that the Steelers extended drives with third-down conversions, that the final drive was a problem, and that the timeout usage late in the fourth quarter was a mistake he would reconsider. He said penalties were on both sides, that the late arrival in Paris was not a factor, and that the team needs to carry forward the positives from the week of practice. On QB Tyler Shough, Moore praised his effort and said he kept the team in the game despite some hard downs. He said the only significant injury concerns are concussion-related ones for CJ Donaldson and Justin Reid, with everyone else expected to be fine. He also addressed WR-related injury news: a player recovering from injury will remain in the training room during the bye, and the team will decide his activation after the bye.

title: Coach John Harbaugh: 'That was a players' win in every way'
headline: Giants' Week 7 win led by J.J. McCarthy's composed first start for the team and Deonte Banks' coverage; Harbaugh gave no fantasy-specific usage news.
summary: Harbaugh credited the players for a win he called a 'player's win in every way,' pointing to blocking, tackling, special teams, and stops in the fourth quarter. He praised J.J. McCarthy's first start for the team, saying the offense ran cleanly with no procedural penalties or clock issues and that McCarthy made strong throws despite a difficult recent stretch. He said Deonte Banks shut down the Texans' top receiver with tight coverage and that Micah McFadden made key tackles, including a tackle for a loss on a sweep. Abdul Carter was described as having taken over the game as a pass rusher and run defender, and Harbaugh said he expects more of that from him. Cam Skattebo and the offensive line were credited for the running game. Harbaugh said the team has lost several players to injury this season and that a player tried to play through an injury before surgery, though he gave no clear status. He said the win gives the team an opportunity but not a guarantee, and that the coaching staff will spend the bye week planning for the next two games, starting with Philadelphia. He also addressed a kicker's missed field goals, saying the kicker is talented and will work through it, and said the team's upcoming stretch is pivotal for the season.

signals.claim: Earned the starting quarterback job for this game after a strong first start; Harbaugh framed the decision as obvious.
signals.note: A solid, composed debut makes him a more reliable fantasy option going forward, and Harbaugh's praise suggests he will keep the role.
signals.quote: It was just an obvious choice.

signals.claim: Shut down the opponent's top receiver with tight coverage; coach said he deserved game-ball recognition.
signals.note: Defensive performance by a cornerback has limited fantasy value, but it signals a strong role and is useful for DFS and defensive scoring.
signals.quote: I probably should have given him a game ball.

signals.claim: Made a bunch of tackles, including a key tackle for a loss on a sweep that set the tone.
signals.note: Heavy tackle production in a larger defensive role supports his value in tackle-based formats.
signals.quote: He had a bunch of tackles.

signals.claim: Took over the game as a pass rusher and was strong against the run; coach expects him to keep growing into a leading defensive player.
signals.note: Carter's pass-rush production and expanded run role boost his value in sack and tackle-based scoring.
signals.quote: I think he took over the game.

signals.claim: Credited with a key running performance, with the offensive line also praised for opening lanes.
signals.note: Positive praise for his effort and the run game supports his workload and fantasy production.
signals.quote: Scat did it.

topics.detail: Harbaugh credited the players for responding to earlier criticism of the defense and for playing with a 'fierce joy' through a close, physical win.

Harbaugh said the team's young kicker has been missing field goals, called it growing pains, and expressed confidence he will get it right; the kicker is not on the roster, so no player signal was recorded.
The team has a bye week, with the next game against Philadelphia followed by a quick turnaround; Harbaugh called the next two games pivotal for the season.
Harbaugh praised a player who scored a winning touchdown after being a healthy scratch for most of the season, but the name was garbled in the captions and was not confidently identified.

title: Aaron Glenn Postgame Press Conference (10/25) | Week 7
headline: Glenn says Garrett Wilson's three-target game is on him and promises more targets; T'Vondre Sweat's knee injury extent is unclear.
summary: Glenn called the loss disappointing and said the defense played poorly in the first half, allowing 21 points on three or four scoring drives. He said the run defense kept letting ball carriers fall forward, and he took responsibility for the defensive concepts. He admitted the team should have used its timeouts late in the first half, and he credited the offense's rhythm for much of the opponent's success. On Garrett Wilson, who had only three targets and reportedly vented on the sideline, Glenn said the game plan calls for getting him the ball and that he would take the blame and work with Geno Smith to get Wilson more targets. He said the team had improved in the second half but still struggled on third down, takeaways, and the red zone on defense. Asked about the 60-yard touchdown, he said it came off a quick out on a corner-cat call, with a roughing-the-passer flag he still needed to review. He defended the program's direction at 2-5, saying the locker room had not quit and that the team is on the right track despite the losing record. On Sweat, he said he learned the extent of the knee injury during the week but gave no clear update.

injuries.detail: Suffered a knee injury in the game; Glenn said he learned the extent during the week but gave no clear update on his status.

signals.claim: Coach says getting Wilson more targets is in the game plan and he will work to make that happen.
signals.note: Wilson's three-target game was a concern, but Glenn's promise is vague, so it is unclear whether his usage will actually rise.
signals.quote: That's in the game plan to make sure he get the ball.

topics.detail: Glenn said the defense struggled early, especially against the run, and took responsibility for the concepts. He also flagged third down, takeaways, and red zone defense as areas needing work.
Glenn admitted the team should have used its timeouts late in the first half to get the ball back before halftime.
Glenn said the team is on the right track despite a 2-5 record and pointed to the locker room's effort as evidence.

title: WATCH: McCarthy on the win over the Saints
headline: McCarthy praised the Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle backfield tandem and said Payton Wilson keeps improving, while the offense's 1-for-4 red zone rate is a clear area to fix.
summary: McCarthy called the Paris trip special and said the road win over New Orleans, 16-10, was valuable because close games teach a team how to make critical plays. He said the team wanted to own the line of scrimmage and hit its rushing goal of 30 attempts, and he credited a young offensive line making consecutive starts. He was happy with the run game and said the team had been moving the chains on third down but needed to stick with the run in those spots. He admitted the red zone, converting only 1 of 4, was not where the team wants to be and needs work. He said the sleep and recovery plan, and the extra reps from a recent overtime game, will factor into preparation for next week. He also said Payton Wilson keeps getting stronger and that the defense's scheme adjustments are helping players get more comfortable. McCarthy said the team is looking forward to Cleveland and that momentum and a 4-0 start in the series matter.

signals.claim: Warren will continue to share a heavy workload with Rico Dowdle in the backfield
signals.note: Coach's comments suggest a two-back rotation that keeps both backs involved, which supports touch volume for each.
signals.quote: anytime we can just line up and give you Jalen and Rico all day

signals.claim: Dowdle will continue to share a heavy workload with Jaylen Warren in the backfield
signals.note: Coach named him alongside Warren as the backfield the team wants to feed, which keeps his touch floor solid.
signals.quote: anytime we can just line up and give you Jalen and Rico all day

signals.claim: Wilson is improving and becoming more comfortable with the scheme adjustments
signals.note: Ongoing growth and a big play in this game point to a larger role on defense, which could help his tackle and splash totals.
signals.quote: Peyton just keeps getting stronger and stronger.

topics.detail: McCarthy acknowledged the offense converted only 1 of 4 trips in the red zone and said touchdowns down there must improve.
The team hit its goal of 30 rushing attempts and gained over 140 yards on the ground; McCarthy said the young offensive line is building on consecutive starts.
Third down was an area needing improvement, but the offense was staying in reasonable third-down situations and running the ball in them.
McCarthy emphasized sleep and recovery and said the weekly plan was adjusted for travel and recent overtime reps, a plan that will carry into next week.
The team is on a three-game win streak and is 4-0 in a series against a division rival, with the next game set for Cleveland.

title: Kyle Shanahan Breaks Down Loss to the Falcons
headline: Jordan Watkins earned praise for his breakout three-week stretch, while four turnovers and sloppy penalties sank the 49ers against Atlanta; McCaffrey's thigh is still unclear.
summary: Shanahan said the loss came down to four turnovers with zero takeaways, which he called the most frustrating part and too sloppy to win. He blamed the turnovers on ball security and said the penalties, especially holds and illegal contact on drives inside the red zone, gave Atlanta big plays. He called the 14-3 swing a turning point: a red-zone fumble, a defensive stop that became a fourth-and-four, and an offsides penalty that gave Atlanta a free first down before a field goal and a late score. He praised the wide receivers and the running game, and said Jordan Watkins has played well for three weeks and made a number of big plays. He acknowledged Watkins fumbled and needs to protect the ball better. On Christian McCaffrey, he said he had not yet talked to him and would wait for the tape after McCaffrey returned from a thigh injury, adding that he seemed all right. He also said a third quarterback getting a late look was not planned; they wanted to give him a shot out of frustration. Special teams drew only mild criticism, with a kickoff that was not placed where it should have been and a missed tackle. He also said he had not discussed the kicker workouts with anyone.

injuries.detail: Left the game with a thigh issue and returned; Shanahan said he seemed all right but would wait for the tape before confirming status.

signals.claim: Has been playing well for three straight weeks and made a number of big plays in this game.
signals.note: Consistent production and a praised role suggest continued heavy target and big-play opportunity, though his fumble is a concern.
signals.quote: he's been playing well here these last three weeks

signals.claim: Needs to throw away the pass on the interception that came after a blitz he didn't see.
signals.note: Two interceptions and a turnover-heavy game raise concern about decision-making and ball security in the short term.
signals.quote: Brock's got to throw that one away.

topics.detail: Shanahan said four turnovers with zero takeaways and sloppy, mistimed penalties were the main reasons for the loss, and he blamed the short week only indirectly.
A backup quarterback got an unplanned look late in the game out of frustration, not as a planned role change; the transcript is unclear on who it was, possibly Upton Stout.
The team worked out some kickers this week, and Shanahan said he had not discussed the outcome and was still discussing the plan.
Shanahan said special teams were not overly frustrating but needed to play better, citing a kickoff that was not placed correctly and a missed tackle that opened up a return.

title: Todd Bowles on Division Win in Carolina: Full-Team Effort | Press Conference
headline: Bowles credits a run-heavy game plan that let Mayfield throw only 11 times, with Gainwell and Tucker sharing the load and Diaby's three sacks as a defensive highlight.
summary: Bowles said the Bucs planned to control time of possession because Carolina's offense is explosive, and he credited the team for converting drives into touchdowns rather than field goals. He praised the defensive line and secondary for working together, with coverage helping the pass rush and the rush helping coverage, and said the front got off the ball early. He called YaYa Diaby's three-sack day a sign that players who had been close to breakout games were arriving, and said the team had talked about the pressure translating into results. Special teams drew praise for a critical punt-return turnover, strong kickoff coverage that kept Carolina out of field position, and the contribution to momentum. On Baker Mayfield, Bowles said he made plays when needed, and that the offensive line and running backs carried the day with 49 runs, which he said was a result they did not plan for going in. Bowles said the run game was working, and he hopes the physical rushing identity becomes consistent, as it reduces blitzes and holding penalties. He was disappointed the defense lacked in the final stretch and that backups were in during that stretch, and he wants a cleaner fourth quarter. He stressed that the first division game is done, with five more to play, and the focus shifts to the non-division games.

injuries.detail: Coming back from a thumb injury; Bowles said the offensive line and running game lightened his workload, limiting him to 11 pass attempts.
Reporter said he missed a little time with a hip injury; Bowles did not dispute it and praised his production in the game.

signals.claim: Breakout three-sack game signals his production will continue
signals.note: Three sacks in one game is a major statistical spike, and Bowles framed it as a sustainable step rather than a fluke.
signals.quote: Yeah, their time is coming. You know, their time is coming.

signals.claim: Part of a three-back rotation that carried the biggest share of the ground game
signals.note: Bowles said the backs were all productive, which supports ongoing carries in a committee-style backfield.

signals.claim: One of three running backs who had strong runs in the win
signals.note: Bowles named him alongside Gainwell as a productive back in a shared rotation, which limits his touch share but keeps him in the mix.

signals.claim: Efficient game managed with a run-heavy plan despite a thumb injury
signals.note: Bowles praised his plays under limited passing volume, which points to continued managed usage while he is coming off the injury.
signals.quote: He made the plays when we needed him.

topics.detail: Bowles praised the coordinated pass rush and coverage that produced three takeaways, but said the unit faded late and backups were on the field at the end.
Bowles credited the punt-return turnover and kickoff coverage that kept Carolina out of midfield with creating momentum for the win.
Bowles wants to make the running game a consistent identity, since it helps limit blitzes and holding penalties; the 49 runs were a result of the run game working rather than the original plan.
Bowles described this as the first division win with five more division games left, and said the focus turns to non-division games.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Saleh blamed the whole team, not Cam Ward alone, for the Browns loss; he praised Ward's late throw to Elic Ayomanor but said he missed some throws, and no injury news was given.
summary: Saleh said the defense was not good enough across the board, especially against the run, with missed tackles, coverage breakdowns on checkdowns, and a pass rush that didn't get home. He called the game a grimy one that Tennessee should have blown open in the first half, and said the team let Cleveland stay in it. He pointed to the goal-line sequences, including a takeaway and a failed push from the inch line, as the 14-point swing that shifted momentum. On Cam Ward, he said he doesn't think it's a quarterback problem, but acknowledged Ward missed some throws he needs to make, while crediting an unbelievable throw to Ayomanor while being hit that tied the game. Saleh said the offense went quiet after its early scores, and he framed the result as the NFL going in waves. He also said the team has to push it in from the inch line and took responsibility for the call on fourth-and-goal. No injuries were discussed in the transcript.

signals.claim: Missed some throws he needs to make; Saleh says the offense problem is not the quarterback alone
signals.note: Ward's accuracy was questioned, but the coach framed the problem as team-wide, so fantasy exposure is not clearly reduced.
signals.quote: He missed some throws. I'm not going to sugarcoat that.

signals.claim: Made a key touchdown catch on a throw from Ward while being hit
signals.note: The coach singled out a play involving Ayomanor as a positive, which supports his involvement in the passing game.
signals.quote: he made up for it with an unbelievable throw to elec while getting hit

topics.detail: Saleh said Cleveland ran the ball well, broke a lot of tackles, and the defense was uncharacteristically poor against the run.
He said the pass rush and pressure designs were not good enough, and coverage was off, especially on checkdowns that went for big yardage.
Saleh said the team must push it in from the inch line and took ownership of the call, while a challenge on a second-and-one sneak was also discussed.
After two early scoring drives, the offense went a couple of quarters without points; Saleh said the team had opportunities to extend the lead but didn't make plays.
